NRL Late Mail: Round 25 - Latrell on hold; Turbo on track
Superstar Latrell Mitchell will target a return in Round 26 against the Titans after his long-awaited comeback was put on hold.
Mitchell has missed 11 games as he battles nerve pain in his lower back which has affected his leg and calf but had been named in the Rabbitohs' extended squad on Tuesday.
"There was a chance (for this week). He trained pretty well but just probably needs another week," coach Wayne Bennett said on Friday.
"We took a cautious approach and we'll give him another week."
Better news for Manly though with Tom Trbojevic a confirmed starter for their clash with the Knights on Saturday.

NRL Casualty Ward: Surgery for Doueihi, Walsh; Turbo good to go
Wests Tigers halfback Adam Doueihi will undergo season-ending surgery that will rule him out of Lebanon's World Cup campaign.
The playmaker dislocated his shoulder in a Round 9 loss to the Sharks and initially delayed surgery in an attempt to kickstart the Tigers finals campaign.
The 28-year-old returned to the field in Round 17 but fresh scans have shown Doueihi requires immediate surgery, with the halfback to go under the knife later this week.
"New scans on Adam's shoulder have showed the time has come to have his reconstruction done. This gives him enough time to be ready for the start of the 2027 season," Wests Tigers head of high performance Peter Moussa said.
Meanwhile, Tigers five-eighth Latu Fainu has suffered a low-grade hamstring injury at training. Fainu was set to return this week after serving a three-game suspension but will now be sidelined for 1-2 weeks with his latest injury.
In positive news, Sunia Turuva has been named on the six-man bench despite suffering a knee injury last week, while Alex Twal is set to return after missing Round 24 due to illness.
Broncos superstar Reece Walsh has had surgery on his ankle and is facing an eight-week recovery time.
Walsh had scans on Sunday which confirmed he had sustained a high-grade syndesmosis injury during the loss to the Warriors on Saturday night.
Warriors fullback Charnze Nicoll-Klokstad has subsequently been banned for two games for a hip drop tackle.
With Australia's World Cup opener against the Kiwis set down for Thursday, October 15 it appears Walsh's chances of representing the Kangaroos are gone.
The Raiders had Simi Sasagi back from a shoulder injury for their clash with the Broncos but lost back-rower Zac Hosking to a hamstring injury during the second half.
South Sydney star Latrell Mitchell will look to return in Round 26 from a nerve injury that has kept him sidelined since Round 11.
The centre has missed 11 games with the injury but was named in the Bunnies' extended squad for this weekend's match against the Warriors before being put on ice once more.
The Rabbitohs have lost Adam Elliott to a groin injury, with the veteran expected to miss two to three weeks with a strained adductor.
Meanwhile, Warriors halfback Luke Metcalf will miss the remainder of the regular season after suffering a hamstring injury in last week's win over Brisbane.
"The timeline for him will be deep into the finals but you never know," coach Andrew Webster said on Thursday.
"I think this is probably the most optimistic I've seen him when he knows he's got a plan and when he knows he wants to attack something."

Rabbitohs vs Warriors Preview & Betting Tips: NRL Round 25 2026
August 21 st 2026, 2:36pm , By: Ben Bridge
Saturday evening at Accor Stadium gives us one of the best games of NRL Round 25 , with South Sydney hosting the Warriors in a matchup carrying major finals implications at both ends of the top eight. The Rabbitohs sit seventh and are trying to lock away their finals position, while New Zealand remain third and level on competition points with Penrith as they chase a top 2 finish and a home final.
Both teams therefore have plenty to play for, but I still lean toward the Warriors despite the disruption in their spine. Luke Metcalf is sidelined with a hamstring injury, Charnze Nicoll-Klokstad is suspended, and Andrew Webster has named Chanel Harris-Tavita at halfback alongside rookie Luke Hanson, who plays just his second NRL game. Taine Tuaupiki moves to fullback. South Sydney are far healthier than earlier in the season, however Latrell Mitchell will not take his place after being named on the extended bench, he has been ruled out.
That inexperienced Warriors halves combination keeps this from becoming a large bet, but their forward pack and season long profile still make Warriors -4.5 the side I want, with their advantage in the forwards and outside backs enough in my opinion.
Rabbitohs vs Warriors Prediction & Tips: 2026 NRL Round 25
Rabbitohs Building Momentum at the Right Time
South Sydney continued their late season surge with a convincing 22-6 victory over Canterbury last Friday, another crucial step toward securing a finals berth after a season that has contained more than its fair share of disruption. The Rabbitohs controlled the contest defensively, restricting the Bulldogs to a single try and again showing that Wayne Bennett has this side peaking at the right stage of the year.
Matt Dufty has been one of the success stories of South Sydney’s resurgence. Against Canterbury he produced 250 running metres, four tackle breaks, a try and a try assist, giving the Rabbitohs the type of support play and yardage they desperately needed during their injury riddled middle of the season.
The bigger improvement has come through the return of their forward leaders. Cameron Murray and David Fifita have both made an immediate impact since returning, and South Sydney look far more capable of sustaining pressure through the middle rather than asking Cody Walker to manufacture everything himself. Souths have won eight consecutive games at Accor Stadium, which makes this a far tougher road assignment for the Warriors than the ladder alone suggests.
The team news is also encouraging. Cody Walker and Jayden Sullivan remain the halves, Brandon Smith starts at hooker and Murray locks a pack featuring Junior Tatola, Keaon Koloamatangi and Fifita. Latrell Mitchell was named to return on the extended bench; however, he is being given one more week before his return next week.
South Sydney are dangerous enough to win this game. The question is whether they can contain a Warriors pack that remains close to full strength despite the disruption in the backline.
Warriors Keep Rolling Despite Injury Setbacks
The Warriors reinforced their premiership credentials last weekend with a dominant 40-6 victory over Brisbane at Suncorp Stadium, controlling the defending premiers from the opening exchanges and never allowing the Broncos into the contest.
That performance was particularly important because the Warriors have continued to absorb injuries without losing their underlying identity. Their season has been built around middle third dominance, strong yardage from their back three, and defensive consistency, and those areas remain intact even with Metcalf and Nicoll-Klokstad unavailable.
James Fisher-Harris and Mitch Barnett give New Zealand one of the best starting prop combinations in the competition, while Wayde Egan remains the crucial link at hooker. Kurt Capewell and Jacob Laban start on the edges, with Erin Clark at lock.

With finals just around the corner, the Warriors will look to get ruthless in their final three regular season games as they chase an elusive first NRL title.
They will meet a resurgent Rabbitohs side having regained their big guns at the perfect time. A new halves combination will take the reins for the 'Wahs', as coach Andrew Webster will take charge of his 100th NRL game as coach.
History
In 40 meetings since 1998, the Bunnies hold a slight advantage with 21 wins to the Warriors 19.
They last met back in June 2025, the Warriors edging out a 36-30 win, courtesy of a late Roger Tuivasa-Sheck double. The Warriors biggest win came in 2006 as they blanked the Bunnies 66-0. The Rabbitohs got their revenge 15 years later with a 60-22 rout on the Sunshine Coast.
Form
Both teams are enjoying hot runs with the Warriors winning their last three on the trot and South Sydney on a two match win streak.
The Warriors were in rampant form against the battling Broncos last weekend, recording a commanding 40-6 win, while the Bunnies beat a strong Bulldogs side 22-6. The Rabbitohs have also recently welcomed back David Fifita and Cam Murray from injury with Latrell Mitchell's comeback imminent.

Rookie Luke Hanson has been handed the number six jersey in just his second match in first grade. Hanson made his debut back in round three against the Knights, with the 22-year-old scoring a try in the 38-12 win.
He will partner Chanel Harris-Tavita, fresh from another contract extension, in the halfback role following Luke Metcalf's departure with a hamstring injury 20 minutes into last Saturday night's match against the Broncos at Suncorp Stadium.
For the Rabbitohs, superstar Latrell Mitchell has been included in the reserves. Wayne Bennett has named former Warrior Euan Aitken in the starting side, replacing Adam Elliott, who has been ruled out with a groin injury. Liam Le Blanc comes onto the bench.

Raiders vs Broncos Preview & Betting Tips: NRL Round 25 2026
August 20 th 2026, 3:36pm , By: Ben Bridge
Friday Night Football at GIO Stadium has far more riding on it than the respective ladder positions suggest, as the Raiders host Brisbane in a matchup loaded with desperation, emotion, and a little revenge. Canberra’s finals hopes remain incredibly faint, but they are still alive. Wins over Brisbane and North Queensland, combined with their Round 26 bye, could get the Raiders to 30 competition points, and leave them praying other results fall their way. Brisbane, meanwhile, have endured one of the worst premiership defences in modern NRL history and are now fighting simply to avoid an unthinkable wooden spoon.
Then there is Josh Papali’i. Friday night will be the Canberra legend’s final home appearance, with GIO Stadium even being temporarily transformed into “Papa’s House” for the occasion. Papali’i has been promoted into the starting front row, and you can guarantee the Raiders faithful will turn this into one of the most emotional home games of the season.
My numbers are not miles away from the current spread, but the circumstances push me toward Canberra. With the Broncos broken, Reece Walsh gone for the season and the Raiders needing a win, I’ll take Canberra -10.5.
Raiders vs Broncos Prediction & Tips: 2026 NRL Round 25
Raiders Refuse to Let Season Die
Canberra looked like a team whose finals hopes were virtually finished heading into last week’s trip to Sharks Stadium, yet they produced one of their gutsiest performances of the season to upset Cronulla 24-20. Against a Sharks side sitting firmly in the top 4 conversation, the Raiders absorbed an early 8-0 deficit, fought their way to an 18-14 halftime lead and then survived a frantic final quarter to keep their season alive.
Joseph Tapine delivered the decisive moment after the Sharks had regained a 20-18 advantage, powering through five defenders to score underneath the posts in the 57th minute. From there, Canberra defended their lead despite Cronulla receiving several opportunities to steal the game late.
It was exactly the type of performance Ricky Stuart would have wanted after the Raiders’ form had again become inconsistent. Canberra have enough attacking talent through Kaeo Weekes, Ethan Strange, Ethan Sanders, Matthew Timoko and Xavier Savage, but their success still starts with the middle. Tapine, Papalii, Zac Hosking and Ata Mariota must generate the field position that allows the young spine to play with freedom.
Morgan Smithies’ failed HIA against Cronulla rules him out this week, forcing Mariota to lock, while Corey Horsburgh returns through the interchange. Simi Sasagi is also back from a shoulder problem, strengthening the centres.
The emotional factor cannot be ignored. Papali’i starts in his final match at GIO Stadium, and Canberra have averaged 35 points across their past four home games. If there is one night where this Raiders side should produce maximum effort for 80 minutes, this is it.
Broncos Hit Rock Bottom in Premiership Defence
Brisbane’s extraordinary collapse continued last Saturday when the Warriors humiliated them 40-6 at Suncorp Stadium. The Broncos trailed 20-0 at halftime and did not score until Xavier Willison crossed in the 64th minute, by which point New Zealand had already put 36 points on the board.
The statistics around Brisbane’s season are becoming almost unbelievable for the defending premiers. They have now lost 12 of their past 13 games, and they are staring down the worst fall from grace by a premiership winning side since Western Suburbs went from premiers to wooden spooners in 1963. Brisbane are now fighting simply to avoid finishing last.
Things somehow got worse against the Warriors when Reece Walsh suffered a syndesmosis injury that has ended his season. Hayze Perham takes over at fullback this week, while Ben Hunt returns to halfback for the first time since Round 18 and Tom Duffy drops to the bench.

There’s plenty at stake for the Panthers, who could drop out of the top two with a loss and need to recover some momentum over the closing three rounds.

The opening Round 8 clash is a crucial encounter for two sides - Newcastle Knights and Wests Tigers - fighting for a top-four berth.
The Tigers arrive in Newcastle full of confidence after a gritty 30-22 win over the Warriors. Lily Rogan starred with a double, while their ability to absorb pressure and capitalise on opportunities proved decisive.
